body:
「21天，我们会做什么？」

前几天发了两篇关于GLP-1和体重管理的内容，收到许多推友的咨询问的最多的是“如果我参加这个训练营，21天具体的内容是什么？”

今天我具体讲一讲这个，我不希望把它变成一个每天打卡报体重的减肥群！我的设想是用21天把体重管理中最重要的几个环节带你完整跑一遍：

第1阶段：先认识自己的体重

开始之前，我们不会急着给你安排一张减肥食谱。先一起看看基础情况：体重、BMI、腰围、既往减重经历、饮食习惯、活动量、睡眠以及目前的治疗情况。

一个BMI 35的人和一个BMI 25但已经反复减重多年的人，面对的问题完全不同，体重管理没有万能模板，因人而异。

第2阶段：学会怎么吃

GLP-1让很多人的食欲下降了。但吃得少并不自动等于吃得对。这21天，我们会重点解决以下5个实际的问题：

1、蛋白质怎么安排？

2、蔬菜和碳水怎么搭配？

3、如果点外卖，该怎么选？

4、聚餐怎么办？

5、食欲很低的时候，怎样避免长期营养摄入不足？

我不希望大家仅仅拿着一个精确到克的食谱生活，更希望你最终形成的是一种对于一日三餐知道该如何调整的能力。

第3阶段：把运动真正融入进生活

减重期间我不希望大家把运动理解成呆板的我今天必须走多少多少公里必须消耗多少卡路里……

运动更重要的价值是帮助我们保持力量、保护肌肉、维持身体功能。所以我们会根据个人情况，把日常活动和力量训练纳入计划。不追求把自己练“废”追求的是能够长期坚持。

第4阶段：每天记录，但不被数字绑架

体重每天都会波动。盐分、碳水、饮水、排便、运动甚至睡眠，都会让体重短期上下变化。

所以我们会定期记录体重、腰围、饮食、活动、睡眠以及身体感受，要看的是过去一两周你的身体趋势到底发生了什么变化而不是某一天“为什么重了0.8公斤”，教你学会看趋势，比每天被体重秤影响情绪更加有意义。

第5阶段：遇到问题怎么办？

这是陪跑真正有价值的地方，有人会遇到食欲太低、有人会便秘、有人会觉得饮食突然变得很无聊，有人会发现体重几天甚至一两周没有明显变化……这个时候很多人会自己加码或者多练一点儿，甚至自行改变药物方案。

我建议这个时间点大家先停下来，复盘一下发生了什么、是不是正常波动、是不是执行出了什么问题，是否需要医生评估目前的情况，然后再决定下一步。

涉及处方药物的调整，始终应该回到正规医疗渠道，由处方医生来根据具体情况判断。

最后7天：开始学习如何维持

这是我最看重的一部分，因为如果21天结束以后，你只是觉得终于减完了！那这个训练营其实没有完成它真正的任务！

我更希望你结营时能够清楚的回答以下6个问题：

1、我的体重正常波动范围是多少？

2、什么情况下我需要警惕反弹？

3、饮食失控以后怎么回来？

4、运动中断以后怎么重新开始？

5、什么时候需要重新评估？

6、如果未来需要调整治疗，我应该与医生讨论什么？

这才是所谓的健康的自我体重管理能力！

所以，这个训练营不会承诺21天一定瘦多少斤，因为每个人的起点、身体状况、治疗方案和执行程度都会不同。

我更愿意承诺的是21天里，我们认真把这套系统跑一遍，让你真正理解怎么吃、怎么动、怎么记录、怎么看数据、怎么面对平台期，以及怎么为长期维持做准备。

GLP-1只是个工具，我希望21天以后你成为一个明确掌握如何管理自己体重的人！这也是我做这个训练营最核心的目的。

Houston VA is now enrolling Veterans in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist used to treat diabetes, as treatment for alcohol use disorder (AUD).  Our VA is one of 18 VA sites nationwide participating in this study.

The study, known as the Cessation or Reduction of Alcohol Consumption in Veterans trial, will enroll more than 600 Veterans. Participants between the ages of 18 and 80 with moderate or severe AUD will receive weekly injections of either semaglutide or a placebo over a 24 week period, followed by a safety follow up. Researchers will track changes in drinking, health, and quality of life to determine whether the medication offers a meaningful new treatment option.

For more information about participation, Veterans can contact us at 713-798-7658.

Nutrition doctor Federica Amati warns going on Ozempic carries a risk of “early onset of DEMENTIA” and “severe brain health issues.”

Specifically, the risk comes from nutritional deficiency. When people go on GLP-1s, the diet that led to the weight gain doesn’t improve, they just eat less of it.

And when that smaller amount of food is still junk food (the case with most people), the brain doesn’t get enough nutrients to thrive.

HOST: “You’ve also seen people lose the weight, come off it, get really hungry, and then find that inevitably they’re therefore going to put the weight on.”

AMATI: “They do. And often it’s quite a big proportion of the weight loss comes back on within the space of six to 12 months.”

HOST: “What about people who are just going to stay on the drug? They’re like, this is magic.”

AMATI: “I’d say it’s quite hard to take these drugs long term and not eat in a way that supports your gut and your body because you will get the side effects.

“If you have any intervention that restricts your food for very long periods of time, you always run into the risks of decreasing your resilience, your immune system really struggling, your brain health struggling, your lean mass or your muscles and your bones struggling.

“There was a patient in the UK who had scurvy, so bleeding gums, people couldn’t understand what was going on. He’d been taking these drugs without any support and just hadn’t been eating fruits and vegetables basically.

“There was a case study of a patient who had started to have really severe brain health issues.

“And the case report described this patient as possibly having early onset of dementia. And then they found out he was just like massively micronutrient deficient for his brain.

“If your dietary quality doesn’t improve on these drugs, then you are definitely going to run into an issue of complete undernourishment.

“So when you take these medications, every single meal counts more than if you weren’t taking them.”

body:
The order of importance for scaling an ecom brand to $10-100 million+ as a @Shopify first brand. (this might be the most comprehensive playbook written on x and is 100% my personal opinion)

Bookmark this for later. **this is not a paid post but I mention a lot of tools and people in this article... and just a note, but none of it was written with AI** 

I also turned this into a graphic with all the KPI's you want to monitor for each section. 

Unit Economics and assumed CAC payback period (if you're a subscription brand) - I would rank this above all other levers of growth, because everything else is a function of this. 

You need to know your  contribution margin per order. COGS, shipping, pick and pack, payment processing and returns. You MUST know this for all of your products to have a target CAC you can grow at. Without it, every scaling decision below is a guess. - learned from the goat @jordanmenard. 

1.) Product market fit - this is a combination of is the product good (what's your Amazon rating?), does it actually do what you say it does and do the consumption economics match your subscription rate you're recommending. (most common cause of cancellations I've seen is... "I have too much product." 

You can scale an 'okay' product with great marketing but you will eventually run into an LTV crisis if re-order rates are too low or churn is too high.

Note on PMF: The brands I've seen grow the fastest have MASSIVE TAM and aren't afraid of saturation. i.e. Weight loss, greens, electrolytes, creatine, etc. 

TAM = total addressable market. 

Example: A niche focus supplement for gamers will not be able to scale like a menopause support supplement will due to size of the markets. 

Lots of ways to find PMF, but two of the easier ones is @kalodata or @H10Software. 

Don't just guess. Test and measure before going all in.

2.) Offer Architecture and pricing - 
Offer = Product + Price frame + Risk reversal + Urgency

Your CAC, CPM's, conversion rate and AOV can all be heavily influenced by this and I think it's one of the things most brands get wrong or never test.  

This is the first thing you need to get right before being able to scale without burning a hole in your credit card. Again... you must know your unit economics to get this right though. I think @jforjacob might be the best at this on x.

3.) Landing pages & CRO (conversion rate optimization) - Offer architecutre is technically part of #3, but other things like social proof, benefit driven copy, authority icons, clinical evidence or statistics to back up your claims, video testimonials, reviews (@judgeme) and strong hero images are important to have structured well.

Beyond that, having landing pages for each stage of awareness. (top of funnel -> advertorial, middle of funnel -> listicle, bottom of funnel -> PDP with strong offers goes without saying.

I've seen @conoritaya completely turn a brand around by just fixing the offer and LP without changing anything else in the brand. 

Taking CVR from 1% to 3% took CAC from $140 to sub $80 using the exact same creatives.

Extra tip on LP's: Gruns, IM8 and other high growth brands will also dedicate PDP's to entire angles for higher congruency from ad->pre-lander->product page. (Example: Gruns Gummies ad about GLP-1 -> listicle on 7 reasons why GLP-1 users are consuming Gruns -> PDP offer.)

You need a dev that can adadpt and move quickly to launch pages. I use @pedro_maradea a lot for these kinds of ad specific LP's. 

4.) Creatives - Could argue this should be above #3 with the Meta andromeda update... since the creative has become the targeting. 

A great creative strategist or creative agency can be worth their weight in gold. The way meta serves up your ads requires you to have a complete funnel architecture hybrid of top of funnel, middle of funnel and bottom of funnel ads at all times. 

You should also add how to use the product, common questions, objections in your ad mix as it'll still show to people that will engage but bring them one step closer to buying.

Statics and AI video: 
@arshsiidhu at DOJO is one of my favorite creative agencies I've worked with so far and crushes ad accounts. His creative strategists are elite level.

Whitelisted Creators Outreach & Onboarding:
@BngrAgency (mine) and @RefunnelApp are great ways to find new creators for partnership ads to get lower CPM's and more new visitors to your brand.

For finding new ads and inspiration:
@Trendtrack_io and @gethookdai are two of my favorite softwares for finding new ads for my brands. 

5.) Media buying strategy - if you want hyper growth, having a strong media buying team that is monitoring the ad account and aggressively scaling / killing ads for cost efficiency is key. 

You have to have all the other pieces in place before this becomes a determinant factor though. I've seen @buffalofink be able to spend 10x more money at the same efficiency with his team.

I've seen @JemBourouhDE do the same, but on Google.

Big note on media buying: Having dialed in attribution and knowing which ads are driving new visitors vs converting existing gets overlooked by most junior media buyers. 

They look at meta and crank budgets on BOF ads when they won't hold spend at higher scales and don't have a @northbeam or @triplewhale to make the correct decisions. 

6.) Retention & Multi Channel Strategy - 
Knowing Blended CAC (your aquisition cost across all channels) allows you to know how much you can spend form day to day. 

Brands that scale to 9 figures are often not just on meta. They're also using TikTok Shop, Snapchat, @AppLovin and especially Amazon.

Meta still remains king of aquisition... but do not discount the halo effect of having an army of affiliates on TikTok and Meta awill have for word of mouth and Amazon growth. 

A Note On Amazon - when you have PMF on meta, you can create your own category on Amazon. Serene Herbs did this with Soursop Bitters and I've seen 2 other brands do this. With scale... you can BECOME a category. 

BASIC RETENTION: SMS/EMAIL/CANCEL FLOWS - A very underrated area of optimization in my opinion, but keeping every customer you acquire with strong win back campaigns and cancel flows can create significant lift with your brand. Reducing every % of MoM churn compounds VERY quickly at scale.

ADVANCED RETENTION: Giving more flavors, more products and more form factors of your existing products for customers to choose from. Meaning: if you have an electrolyte and you only have two flavors, give them more to try. Give them a reason to keep coming back and buying new things from you. 

If you have a gummy, put it in a capsule or a liquid or a stick pack. Gummy LTV is usually 4-5 months and then it drops off pretty hard. Different people like different ways of consuming your product. 

I work with some great manufacturing partners for all these form factors if you need some for your brand. Feel free to DM and I can connect.

I learned a lot from @iamshackelford at @CommerceRound on what makes people want to come back to brands. Highly recommend hearing his talks and following him on x.

7.) Logistics and finance - Having a great 3PL, packaging, inventory forecasting, strong terms with your manufacturer and knowing that your manufacturer can match your scale of growth, CAC:LTV ratio dialed in on 3 month, 6 month and 12 month cohorts with look back tracking. 

I've loved @glenwomble and robo3pl for my brands so far. 

8.) Customer service - Being responsive, strong support, putting the customer first all keep people coming back and give you stronger reviews. 

Brand / Organic - In 2026, I think these have been largely forgotten and are probably the MOST neglected ways to scale. One viral video can change a business overnight and founder ads are still the strongest performing ads that rarely fatigue. 

I have a strong theory that the brands with good organic have better CPM's than brands with no organic presence. 

One way I've seen this work well is with strong top of funnel celebrity / creators that have a strong story. I think that @ChrisLangSocial and @theisaacmed are two of the best organic marketers in the game.  

For new ecom operators, I think that @9operators is one of the best resources for new trends in terms of growth and scaling ecom brands. 

NOT INCLUDING RETAIL IN THIS ARTICLE. THAT IS A COMPLETELY SEPEARTE TOPIC... BUT SHOULD BE ADDED IN MULTICHANNEL.

Open to hearing others opinions on what they believe the strongest lever to scale is, but this is what I've seen peeking beneath the hood of 50+ brands at all different stages.

body:
Reta stop working?

Your GLP-1 might not be the problem.

Your BAC water could be.

A lot of people focus on the peptide, the dose, or the source and completely overlook the water used to reconstitute it.

Once bacteriostatic water is opened, it has a limited usable window. Many multi-dose vials are typically discarded around 28 days after first puncture.

Why?

Every time the stopper is punctured, there’s another opportunity for contamination. Storage conditions matter too. Heat, poor handling, repeated punctures, or using an old vial can all affect the integrity of what’s inside.

A few simple things to keep in mind:

• Write the open date on the vial

• Follow the manufacturer’s storage instructions

• Don’t assume an opened vial is good indefinitely

• Use clean handling practices every time the stopper is accessed

• When in doubt, replace it

Sometimes the thing people overlook most is the simplest part of the process.

Congressman Tom Oliverson on 340b, the No Surprises Act, gold carding, and more

In this episode of the Doctor's Lounge, Anthony DiGiorgio speaks with Hon. Tom Oliverson, MD, Texas State Representative for House District 130 and chair of the House Republican Caucus. Dr. Oliverson shares how he moved from medicine into public service, why practicing physicians should remain involved in policymaking, and what Texas is doing to address healthcare affordability. They also dig into 340B, prior authorization reform, and the origins of the No Surprises Act.

DataMeds AI, Inc. (@DataMEDSAI) (@Nasdaq : $MEDS) completed the acquisition of Helomics Corporation, the Pittsburgh-based artificial intelligence cancer diagnostics laboratory business of Axe Compute Inc. (Nasdaq: $AGPU). Helomics applies artificial intelligence to real-world tumor data to support drug discovery and cancer treatment decisions.

DataMeds AI, Inc. is a B2i Digital (@b2idigital ) Featured Company. See the company's in-depth profile at: https://t.co/du3clZI66q

The acquisition brings a certified laboratory, a contract research services business and operational capital to DataMeds:

• Helomics acquired from Axe Compute in exchange for common shares and an acquisition note of DataMeds, for a total purchase value of $1.5 million

• The Helomics CLIA/CAP-certified clinical laboratory, the Predictive Oncology CRO central lab services business and $1.5 million in cash

• No third party debt requiring repayment and no outstanding, unpaid accounts payable outside of ongoing monthly operational expenses

• Under DataMeds' ownership, Helomics is expected to expand beyond tumor molecular profiling and chemosensitivity testing into cancer screening and traditional CLIA laboratory services

Regarding the expanded scope, Gerald Commissiong, Interim Co-CEO of DataMeds, stated: "Given Helomics' rich history of pioneering innovative solutions in the $40 billion U.S. cancer diagnostic and treatment solutions market, we intend to expand the scope of DataMEDS broader services with this acquisition beyond GLP-1 agonist side effects and Long COVID, into cancer diagnosis and treatment."

Read the full release: https://t.co/VM3G6AoGhW
